name: Creamy Shrimp Lasagna
description: Layered lasagna with garlicky shrimp, creamy béchamel, tomato sauce and melted cheese.

source.note: No accessible written recipe was provided; measurements and method are Food Expert-developed.

steps.title: Make tomato sauce
steps.text: Sauté diced onion in half the oil. Add half the garlic, tomato sauce and herbs. Simmer until slightly thickened.

steps.title: Sear shrimp
steps.text: Pat shrimp dry, season with salt, pepper and optional chili. Sear in remaining oil with garlic for 1–2 minutes per side, just until opaque. Remove immediately.

steps.title: Make creamy sauce
steps.text: Melt butter, whisk in flour for 1 minute, then gradually whisk in milk and cream. Simmer until thick. Whisk in cream cheese and Parmesan; adjust seasoning.

steps.title: Prepare pasta
steps.text: Cook regular sheets until flexible, or use no-boil sheets if your sauce is loose enough.

steps.title: Layer
steps.text: In a 23 × 33 cm dish, layer tomato sauce, pasta, shrimp and creamy sauce. Repeat for 3 layers. Finish with creamy sauce and mozzarella.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Cover and bake 20 minutes. Uncover and bake 10–15 minutes more until bubbling and golden.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Rest before slicing so the creamy layers set.

donenessCues: Sauce bubbles at the edges.
Top is melted and golden.
Pasta is tender in the center.
Shrimp are opaque and firm, not rubbery.
chefNotes: Do not overcook shrimp before baking.
Pat shrimp dry for better browning.
Resting is essential for clean slices.
commonMistakes: Overcooked shrimp
Too little sauce
Skipping the resting period
Over-salting after adding cheese
substitutions: Evaporated milk can replace part of the cream.
Frozen shrimp are fine if thawed and dried well.
Canned tomato sauce can replace passata.
storage: Refrigerate promptly. Reheat until thoroughly hot; oven or air fryer gives the best texture.

name: Ultimate Cheeseburger Wellington
description: A cheeseburger wrapped in golden puff pastry with cheddar, caramelized onions, pickles and burger sauce.

source.note: The supplied Reel did not provide an accessible written recipe. Measurements are Food Expert-developed.

steps.title: Make the burger sauce
steps.text: Mix mayonnaise, ketchup, yellow mustard, chopped pickles, pickle juice, garlic powder, onion powder and black pepper. Refrigerate.

steps.title: Caramelize the onions
steps.text: Cook thinly sliced onion with oil, butter and salt until deeply golden, soft and jammy. Add small splashes of water if sticking. Add optional sugar if desired. Cool completely.

steps.title: Form the patties
steps.text: Gently mix ground beef with salt, pepper, garlic powder, onion powder and Worcestershire sauce. Divide into four approximately 125 g portions and shape into patties.

steps.title: Sear the patties
steps.text: Sear about 2–3 minutes per side for a browned crust. Transfer to a clean plate and cool; the burgers will finish cooking in the oven.

steps.title: Prepare the pastry
steps.text: Keep puff pastry cold. Roll only as needed so each piece can fully enclose one burger without stretching.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Layer patty, cheddar, burger sauce, pickles and caramelized onions. Leave about 2–3 cm of clean pastry around the edge. Brush edge with egg wash, fold, seal firmly and place seam-side down.

steps.title: Chill
steps.text: Chill the assembled Wellingtons to firm the pastry fat and help maintain shape.

steps.title: Egg wash and vent
steps.text: Brush with beaten egg and water. Sprinkle sesame seeds and optional flaky salt. Cut 2–3 small vents on top.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake in a fully preheated oven until deeply golden and crisp. Check the beef center with a thermometer; ground beef should reach at least 71°C.

steps.title: Rest and serve
steps.text: Rest before cutting. Serve with burger sauce, crispy fries, extra pickles or a fresh salad.

donenessCues: Pastry is deeply golden, crisp and visibly flaky.
Beef center reaches at least 71°C.
Caramelized onions are soft, glossy, deeply golden and jammy.
Cheese is melted and mostly contained within the pastry.
chefNotes: Keep pastry cold; warm filling can melt the pastry fat before baking.
Do not overfill with sauce or wet ingredients.
Cool the patties and onions before assembly.
Resting improves slicing and keeps the filling from rushing out.
commonMistakes: Soggy pastry from warm or wet filling.
Wellington bursting because of overfilling or weak seams.
Dry beef from cooking the patties too long before baking.
Raw pastry from pastry being too thick or an oversized filling.
substitutions: Use locally available frozen puff pastry.
Regular cheddar works well; mature cheddar gives a stronger cheeseburger flavor.
Dill pickles are preferred; sour cucumber pickles can work.
If Worcestershire sauce is unavailable, a small amount of soy sauce can be used, creating a more Asian-leaning flavor.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers promptly. Reheat in an oven or air fryer for better pastry texture; reheat until thoroughly hot.

name: Crispy Salmon Cucumber Sushi + Sushi Dessert
description: Crispy glazed salmon over cucumber-and-sushi-rice bases, plus fruit-filled dessert sushi with chocolate and crunchy crumbs.

source.note: No written recipe was supplied; measurements and method are Food Expert-developed from the visual sequence.

steps.title: Cook and season rice
steps.text: Rinse rice, cook with water, rest 10 minutes. Dissolve rice vinegar, sugar and salt, then fold into hot rice. Cool to room temperature.

steps.title: Make salmon glaze
steps.text: Mix soy sauce, honey, sesame oil and garlic. Cut salmon into thick pieces and coat lightly.

steps.title: Crisp salmon
steps.text: Sear salmon in a lightly oiled pan until browned and cooked through. Brush with glaze during the final minute.

steps.title: Prepare cucumber
steps.text: Halve cucumbers lengthwise, scoop out watery seeds, pat dry and trim a thin strip underneath so each half sits flat.

steps.title: Build savory sushi
steps.text: Press rice into cucumber halves. Add spicy mayo, avocado, spring onion and crispy salmon. Finish with sesame.

steps.title: Slice
steps.text: Use a sharp damp knife to cut into thick pieces. Serve immediately.

steps.title: Make dessert filling
steps.text: Beat cream cheese with honey and vanilla until smooth.

steps.title: Prepare dessert wrapper
steps.text: Spread a thin crepe or soft tortilla with chocolate spread and press crushed graham crumbs into the surface.

steps.title: Fill and roll dessert
steps.text: Spread cream cheese over the wrapper. Arrange banana, mango, strawberries, raspberries and kiwi in rows. Roll tightly.

steps.title: Chill and cut
steps.text: Chill seam-side down until firm. Slice into rounds; coat with coconut or crumbs and drizzle with chocolate if desired.

donenessCues: Rice is tender but holds its shape.
Salmon is browned outside and opaque through the center.
Cucumber stays crisp and sturdy.
Dessert roll is firm enough to slice cleanly.
chefNotes: Dry cucumber thoroughly.
Cool rice before filling.
Pat salmon dry for the best crust.
This is sushi-inspired rather than traditional Japanese sushi.
commonMistakes: Overfilling cucumber
Wet cucumber or warm rice
Dry overcooked salmon
Cutting dessert before chilling
substitutions: Japanese mayo can replace regular mayo.
Firm Philippine cucumber can work after removing seeds.
A thin crepe can replace tortilla.
Digestive biscuits can replace graham crackers.
storage: Best eaten immediately. Refrigerate cooked salmon and rice promptly; assembled cucumber sushi loses texture quickly.

description: Creamy, garlicky, buttery and spicy pasta layered with caramelized red onion, chili oil, soy, honey, cream, smoky sausage and garlic-butter shrimp.

source.note: Public article description was accessible; the full paid recipe was not. This app entry is a Food Expert reconstruction from the public description and the previously approved FE-004 version.

steps.title: Caramelize the onions
steps.text: Cook the sliced red onions with a little butter and oil until deeply softened, jammy and golden. Stir often enough to prevent scorching.

steps.title: Build garlic butter
steps.text: Cook the garlic gently in butter until very fragrant and softened; avoid browning the garlic aggressively.

steps.title: Cook sausage and shrimp
steps.text: Brown the sausage, then sear the shrimp in garlic butter until just opaque and cooked through. Remove shrimp so it stays tender.

steps.title: Make the chili cream sauce
steps.text: Add chili oil, soy sauce, honey and cream. Stir in caramelized onions and simmer gently until silky.

steps.title: Cook pasta and combine
steps.text: Cook spaghetti al dente. Reserve pasta water, then toss pasta into the sauce, adding pasta water gradually until glossy and clingy. Fold sausage and shrimp back in.

steps.title: Finish
steps.text: Finish with parsley, black pepper and an extra drizzle of chili oil. Serve immediately.

donenessCues: Shrimp is opaque and firm but still juicy.
Sauce coats the spaghetti in a glossy layer rather than pooling thinly.
Garlic smells sweet and aromatic, not burnt.
Caramelized onions are soft and jammy.
chefNotes: Control the heat carefully once cream is added; a gentle simmer gives a smoother sauce.
Reserve pasta water before draining because the starch helps emulsify the sauce.
Add shrimp back near the end to prevent overcooking.
commonMistakes: Burning garlic by using high heat.
Boiling the cream aggressively.
Overcooking shrimp while finishing the pasta.
Adding too much soy sauce before tasting.
substitutions: Heavy cream or all-purpose cooking cream can be used.
Calamansi is not a direct substitute for the sauce acidity here; use a tiny splash only at the table if desired.
Pechay or spinach can replace parsley as a vegetable addition, but the texture changes.
storage: Refrigerate leftovers promptly in an airtight container and use within 3 days. Reheat gently with a splash of water or cream.
name: Chili Garlic Cream Pasta

description: A crisp, cheesy breakfast triangle made from a tortilla wrapped around cheese batons, egg, tomatoes and fresh herbs.

source.note: Recipe text supplied by the user.

ingredients.name: Large whole wheat tortilla or thin flatbread
Extra beaten egg for egg wash
Mixed black and white sesame seeds

steps.title: Preheat
steps.text: Preheat oven or air fryer to 180°C. Line a baking tray if using an oven.

steps.title: Build the triangle
steps.text: Lay tortilla flat and arrange the three cheese sticks in the center as a triangle.

steps.title: Fold and secure
steps.text: Fold the tortilla edges over the cheese to form a triangular boat. Secure the three overlapping corners with toothpicks.

steps.title: Fill
steps.text: Crack one egg into the center. Add herbs, tomatoes and shredded cheese.

steps.title: Egg wash and garnish
steps.text: Brush folded tortilla edges with beaten egg and sprinkle with sesame seeds. Season the center.

steps.title: Bake
steps.text: Bake until the tortilla is crisp and golden, cheese is melted and the egg reaches your preferred doneness.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Cool briefly, remove all toothpicks carefully, slice and serve.

donenessCues: Tortilla edges are golden and crisp.
Cheese is visibly melted.
Egg white is set; yolk is cooked to your preference.
chefNotes: Use a thin tortilla so the folded edges crisp before the egg overcooks.
Toothpicks are essential for holding the triangle shape during baking.
commonMistakes: Overfilling the center and causing the egg to spill.
Forgetting to remove toothpicks before serving.
Using a very thick flatbread that stays doughy.
substitutions: Mozzarella or mild cheddar for the cheese sticks.
Parsley, cilantro or spinach for herbs.
Pechay is not ideal here because it releases more water; use spinach instead if substituting.
storage: Best eaten immediately. Refrigerate leftovers and reheat in an oven/air fryer rather than a microwave for better crispness.
name: Crispy Egg & Cheese Tortilla Triangles

description: Creamy, spicy Buldak noodles coated in a cheese-and-mayo sauce and topped with shrimp, crispy sausage and a fried egg.

source.note: Recipe text supplied by the user.

ingredients.name: Samyang Buldak instant noodles, Carbonara or Cheese

steps.title: Cook toppings
steps.text: Pan-fry shrimp until pink and cooked through. Fry scored sausages until browned and crisp at the edges. Fry the egg to your liking. Set aside.

steps.title: Boil noodles
steps.text: Cook noodles according to package directions. Reserve about ¼ cup starchy noodle water before draining.

steps.title: Build creamy sauce
steps.text: In the warm pot add American cheese, mayonnaise, ketchup, half the green onions, the Buldak powder packet and liquid sauce packet.

steps.title: Emulsify
steps.text: Add a splash of hot noodle water and stir vigorously until the cheese melts into a thick creamy sauce.

steps.title: Toss noodles
steps.text: Add drained noodles and toss until evenly coated.

steps.title: Melt mozzarella
steps.text: Sprinkle mozzarella over the noodles and cover briefly until melted.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Top with shrimp, sausages and fried egg. Finish with remaining green onions and optional chili crisp or sesame seeds.

donenessCues: Shrimp is opaque and just cooked.
Sausages have browned edges.
Sauce is smooth and clings to noodles.
Egg reaches your desired doneness.
chefNotes: Use low heat for the cheese sauce so it stays smooth.
Starchy noodle water is the bridge between the cheese and the spicy sauce.
commonMistakes: Boiling the cheese sauce hard.
Adding all the water at once and making it thin.
Overcooking the shrimp.
substitutions: Hotdog or cocktail sausages work well.
Cheddar can replace American cheese but melts differently.
Pechay can be added for a vegetable component.
storage: Eat immediately for best texture. Refrigerate leftovers promptly and use within 2 days; reheat gently with a splash of water.
name: Creamy Cheesy Buldak Noodles with Shrimp & Sausage

description: Crispy-edged smash burgers cooked directly onto flour tortillas, finished with melted cheese, burger sauce and fresh toppings.

source.note: Recipe text supplied by the user.

steps.title: Prep patties
steps.text: Divide beef into two portions and press each directly onto one tortilla, covering the tortilla to the edges. Season generously.

steps.title: Smash
steps.text: Place tortilla meat-side down on a hot skillet or griddle. Press firmly to maximize contact and develop a browned crust.

steps.title: Flip and melt
steps.text: Flip carefully. Add cheese and cook until the tortilla is toasted and the cheese melts.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Spread burger sauce over the cheese, then add lettuce, onion and tomato.

steps.title: Serve
steps.text: Fold into taco shape and serve immediately.

donenessCues: Beef has a deep brown crust and crisp lacy edges.
Cheese is fully melted.
Tortilla is toasted but still foldable.
chefNotes: The pan must be hot before the meat hits it.
Do not keep moving the tortilla during the first side; uninterrupted contact builds the crust.
commonMistakes: Using very lean beef and getting a dry patty.
Crowding the pan.
Flipping before the crust develops.
substitutions: Ground pork or chicken can work, but the crust and fat level will change.
Corn tortillas can be used, though they behave differently and are less forgiving for the smash technique.
storage: Best served immediately. Refrigerate cooked leftovers promptly and reheat in a skillet or air fryer.
name: Smash Burger Tacos

description: A creamy spicy ramen bowl with gnocchi, mushrooms and bok choy, built from a mayo-egg seasoning base and finished with a crispy fried egg and black vinegar.

source.note: Recipe text supplied by the user.

steps.title: Boil solids
steps.text: Cook ramen, gnocchi, mushrooms and bok choy in boiling water until tender.

steps.title: Build base
steps.text: In the serving bowl whisk Kewpie mayo, raw egg, ramen seasoning and chili crisp into a thick paste.

steps.title: Temper with hot water
steps.text: Ladle about 1–1½ cups hot cooking water into the bowl gradually while whisking vigorously to create a creamy broth.

steps.title: Assemble
steps.text: Drain the noodles, gnocchi and vegetables and fold them into the broth.

steps.title: Garnish
steps.text: Top with a fried egg, extra chili crisp, black vinegar and sesame seeds.

donenessCues: Broth is creamy and emulsified rather than watery.
Ramen remains springy.
Gnocchi is tender without falling apart.
Fried egg is crisp at the edges.
chefNotes: Add hot water slowly to temper the raw egg and prevent scrambling.
Black vinegar cuts the richness of the mayo and egg.
Do not overcook the ramen before combining with the broth.
commonMistakes: Pouring boiling water in all at once and scrambling the egg.
Overcooking gnocchi.
Adding too much seasoning packet before tasting.
substitutions: Regular mayonnaise for Kewpie.
Pechay for bok choy.
Rice vinegar can replace black vinegar, but the flavor is brighter and less malty.
Chili garlic oil can replace chili crisp.
storage: Because this recipe uses an egg tempered with hot water, use pasteurized egg when available for the safest result. Eat immediately; refrigerate leftovers promptly and use within 1 day.
name: Creamy Chili-Crisp Ramen with Gnocchi
